entry.title: Peer Complexity in Big History
entry.summary: Employing the framework of cosmological periodization of Adams and Laughlin’s The Five Ages of the Universe as an extension of Big History, we will focus on the kinds of emergent complexity that appear to characterize the current age of star formation (the Stelliferous Era). We will define a conception of peer emergent complexity and place the emergent complexities familiar to human beings—life, consciousness, intelligence, technology, civilization—within this context of peer emergent complexity. Placing Earth-originating emergent complexities within a cosmologically conceived class of peer emergent complexities converges on a less anthropocentric conception of what we can expect to find in the pursuit of biosignatures and technosignatures, which categories may prove to be too restrictive. The consequences of these considerations for SETI will then be explored, with stronger and weaker formulations of the Fermi paradox given.

entry.title: Rubin Observatory LSST Transients and Variable Stars Roadmap
entry.summary: Abstract The Vera C. Rubin Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) holds the potential to revolutionize time domain astrophysics, reaching completely unexplored areas of the Universe and mapping variability time scales from minutes to a decade. To prepare to maximize the potential of the Rubin LSST data for the exploration of the transient and variable Universe, one of the four pillars of Rubin LSST science, the Transient and Variable Stars Science Collaboration, one of the eight Rubin LSST Science Collaborations, has identified research areas of interest and requirements, and paths to enable them. While our roadmap is ever-evolving, this document represents a snapshot of our plans and preparatory work in the final years and months leading up to the survey’s first light.
